the observed multiple populations in open clusters of intermediate ages are likely to be the result of a combination of differential reddening and stellar rotation, and not the result of multiple populations.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a detailed analysis of stellar rotation is essential for the correct interpretation of multiple-population features in intermediate-age open clusters.
the appearance of a star cluster’s CMD can be significantly influenced by differential reddening and stellar rotation.
the interpretation of CMDs of open clusters should be performed cautiously, especially when the cluster is located near the plane of the Milky Way.
